The Emerson results indicate a wider edge for Democrats than some other findings.

Decision Desk HQ’s polling averages put Democrats at an advantage of roughly 4 points, with around 46 percent support to the GOP’s 42 percent. That includes July polling from YouGov/The Economist, which found Democrats up by 5 points in its latest survey, and from Morning Consult, which found Democrats up by just 3 points — and it marks a slight tightening of the margin since last month. [...] A national survey from Emerson College Polling found 53 percent of voters sided with the generic Democrat, up 3 points from last month, while 42 percent sided with the Republican, up 2 points from last month.

results.content:
Among registered voters, Democrats led the generic congressional ballot 42 percent to 37 percent. Independents favored Democratic candidates by 12 points.

Reuters/Ipsos surveyed 4,505 U.S. adults nationwide online July 30-August 3. The poll had a margin of error of 2 percentage points.

## Competitive Districts Show Similar Pattern

New analysis from Economist/YouGov suggested Democratic strength extends beyond heavily blue districts.
